subject: zoology
question_text: What do you call the locomotor structures of Nereis? Why is Nereis called a polychaete?

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The locomotor structures
steps.why: The parapodium is a flap of the body wall itself, which is why one organ can serve both for movement and for the exchange of gases.
common_mistakes: Writing setae. The setae are carried ON the parapodia; the locomotor organ is the parapodium.
Writing that parapodia are present on a few segments only. They are present on every segment.
steps.memory_tip: Para-podium means side-foot: a foot on the side of each segment.
steps.margin_note: Name the organ, say where it lies and what it does. Three or four lines.
lines: The locomotor structures of Nereis are called
A parapodium is a flat, paired outgrowth on
the side of every body segment.
The parapodia are used for swimming and for
They are thin and hold many blood vessels, so
they also take part in respiration.

steps.label: Why it is a polychaete
steps.why: The class name is a count of setae, so the answer is complete only when the number of setae per segment is stated.
common_mistakes: Writing that the setae lie on the body wall. In Nereis they are carried on the parapodia.
Answering 'many setae' alone. Say that they are borne on the parapodia of every segment.
steps.memory_tip: Poly-chaeta is many setae; oligo-chaeta is few setae. Count the setae, name the class.
steps.margin_note: Explain the class name from the word itself. Two or three lines.
lines: Nereis is called a polychaete because every
Poly means many and chaeta means seta, so the
name records the large number of setae.
An earthworm has only a few setae in each
segment, and it is therefore an oligochaete.

insider_note: The second mark is for taking the word apart — poly and chaeta — so write the meaning of the name, not just the fact that setae are present.
